# Get-ZbxMap

## SYNOPSIS

Gets the network maps that draw hosts and their problems.

## SYNTAX

### All (Default)

```
Get-ZbxMap [-Limit <int>] [-SortField <string[]>] [-Id <ulong[]>] [-User <ZabbixReference<ZabbixUser>[]>] [-SelectElements] [-SelectShapes] [-SelectLines] [-SelectLinks] [-SelectIconMap] [-SelectUrls] [-SelectUsers] [-SelectUserGroups] [-Editable] [-InputObject <PSObject>] [-SortOrder <ZabbixSortOrder[]>] [-Search <Hashtable>] [-SearchByAny] [-StartSearch] [-ExcludeSearch] [-SearchWildcardsEnabled] [-CountOutput] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-First <UInt64>] [-Skip <UInt64>] [-IncludeTotalCount] [<CommonParameters>]
```

```

```

## DESCRIPTION

A network map draws hosts, host groups, triggers and other maps as icons joined by links, colored by the problems behind them. The Get-ZbxMap cmdlet reads them with map.get: all of them up to -Limit, by name with -Name (* and ? are wildcards), by id with -Id or from the pipeline, or with the whole map.get selection in -Filter. -User narrows the result to the network maps of the given users, each a name, an id or a piped object. It writes ZabbixMap objects, with their related objects when a -Select switch asks for them, or, with -CountOutput, the number of matches; it needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Get a network map by name

```powershell
Get-ZbxMap -Name 'Office map'
```

Gets the network map named Office map. A * or ? in -Name makes it a search, so -Name 'Office*' gets every network map whose name starts with Office.

### Example 2: Get the network maps of a user

```powershell
Get-ZbxMap -User 'jdoe'
```

Gets the network maps of the user jdoe. -User takes a name, an id or an object; a user piped from Get-ZbxUser binds to it by its UserId property.

### Example 3: Search network maps with a filter

```powershell
Get-ZbxMap -Filter @{ search = @{ name = 'Office' }; limit = 10 }
```

-Filter takes the whole map.get selection, keyed by the API's field names: here at most ten network maps whose name contains Office.
